parts.text:
You design Thai language lesson scenarios. Given vocabulary words, create a vivid realistic scene where two Thai adult friends (not family members) naturally use these words. Characters A and B are friends or acquaintances — never parent/child, never siblings.

Vocabulary: รถเมล์=bus, ยาว=long, ครั้ง=time(s), occasion, คุ้ม=to be worthwhile, ทางเข้า=entrance, ควร=should, กังวล=to worry, รีบ=hurry, หวัง=hope, คู่=pair/couple, ชิ้น=piece/classifier, ไฟ=light/electricity, ต้องการ=want, need (formal), สามารถ=be able to (formal), เล่า=tell

Return ONLY valid JSON (no markdown):
{"scene":"2-sentence scene in English","characterA":"Thai man name and role","characterB":"Thai woman name and role","nameA_th":"A's name written in Thai script exactly as used in the Thai lines (e.g. สมชาย)","nameB_th":"B's name written in Thai script exactly as used in the Thai lines (e.g. นิดา)","opening":"Natural Thai greeting A says to B (must end ครับ). MUST warmly acknowledge the person — สวัสดีครับ is fine, or casual: วันนี้เป็นยังไงบ้างครับ, นานไม่ได้เจอกันเลยครับ, มาถึงแล้วเหรอครับ, เพิ่งมาถึงเหรอครับ, ว่างไหมครับ. BANNED: ไปไหนมาครับ (interrogation, not greeting). Make the other person feel welcomed.","opening_phonetic":"full romanisation of opening","opening_english":"English translation of opening (omit particle)","opening_prompt":"One sentence — ALWAYS use both character names (e.g. Somchai greets Nida and says it has been a long time). Never use vague he/she without naming the characters.","reply":"B greets A back and responds to what A said. ONE simple sentence only — must end with a single ค่ะ or คะ. Do NOT ask if something is wrong, if he has problems, or if he is troubled. Keep it warm and positive.","reply_phonetic":"full romanisation of reply","reply_english":"English translation of reply (omit particle)","reply_prompt":"Use B's name ONCE to open, then she/he only — NEVER repeat B's own name twice in one sentence. e.g. Nida greets Somchai back and says SHE is doing well (NOT: says Nida is doing well). No job titles.","closing":"Natural Thai parting A says to B to end the conversation (must end ครับ). Vary it — do not always use แล้วเจอกัน. Draw on: ไว้เจอกันใหม่ครับ, ดูแลตัวเองด้วยนะครับ, เดินทางปลอดภัยนะครับ, ขอให้เป็นวันที่ดีนะครับ, โชคดีนะครับ, แล้วคุยกันนะครับ, ฝันดีครับ. Must fit the time of day and the scene.","closing_phonetic":"full romanisation of closing","closing_english":"English translation of closing (omit particle)","closing_prompt":"One sentence naming A, e.g. Somchai says goodbye to Nida and tells her to take care.","closing_reply":"B's short parting back to A. ONE sentence, ends with ค่ะ. Should differ from A's wording — if A says see you again, B might wish him a safe trip.","closing_reply_phonetic":"full romanisation","closing_reply_english":"English translation (omit particle)","closing_reply_prompt":"One sentence naming B once, then she/he."}

CRITICAL: whatever Thai name/nickname you use in the opening and reply Thai fields, use the SAME name (romanized) in all English fields. No different English name for the same character.
